title: Throughput Assurance Annex: graduated credits & autoscale arbitration language
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Purpose: define a concise contractual annex and machine-readable SLO interpretation that (a) quantifies throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers, (b) specifies graduated crediting for partial degradations, and (c) describes the autoscale arbitration behavior and mitigation steps when reserved pools are constrained. The deliverable is a short legal-friendly clause set plus an engineering appendix that maps metrics to credit calculation and automated escalation actions.
acceptance_criteria: Contract annex drafted in plain-English and legal-ready format (<= 2 pages).
Credit calculation formula specified with worked examples for 24h / 7d windows.
Autoscale arbitration rules documented with decision tree and fallback order (region -> model-variant -> burst-pool).
Engineering appendix links metric names to observability dashboards and defines the canonical error budget burn pipeline.
Sign-off obtained from Legal, Revenue Ops, and Platform Reliability Engineering.
decisions: Use a graduated credit schedule (0-10%, 10-30%, >30% SLA shortfall) rather than a binary pass/fail credit to reduce disputes for transient throttling.
Define the primary SLI as 95th percentile tokens-served-per-second per committed GPU-equivalent across the billing window; fallback SLI is median-latency increase when autoscale engaged.
Autoscale arbitration will prefer intra-region model-variant fallback before cross-region failover to limit customer-facing latency impact.
Credits are applied to the following billing cycle unless customer requests immediate crediting via support ticket within 30 days.

SRE to implement tagging hook in observability pipeline so credit decisions reference incident IDs (ENG-24101).
Billing to confirm cap and write-up for monthly credit limit (Revenue Ops) and acceptance of applied credits in invoice system.

notes: Trade-offs considered: more granular crediting increases disputes but better aligns cost with customer experience; simpler binary SLAs reduce disputes but can over-penalize brief platform noise.
We intentionally decoupled the SLI used for crediting from internal incident severity to avoid conflating customer impact with internal pager noise.
Autoscale arbitration must be deterministic and explainable for post-mortem and billing reconciliation — we will document the exact rule priority in the engineering appendix.
